reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount helper and takes the tolerance from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in #shared/rules, which rule matching also uses, instead of hard-coding 7.5%.

duplication.why: The approximate worst case is written once inside the shared helper, and schedule-template.ts drops its own isbetween dispatch in favour of the helper.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the shared module that every client and server call site already uses for expected amounts.

scope.why: Every edit either threads the operator to an existing caller or changes the helper itself.

maintainability.why: There is one definition that every planning path uses; amountOp is typed as a plain string rather than the operator type, and the schedule editor passes hard-coded operator literals to opt out of the approximate rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: none; every getScheduledAmount call passes the operator, and the tolerance comes from getApproxNumberThreshold

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount (with getApproxNumberThreshold), called by Balance, SchedulesTable, the mobile schedules views, useScheduleEdit, api.ts, schedule-template.ts, schedules/app.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions
